interactions.title: Lady Eventide withdraws into Seeker’s hair

DM: Suddenly, now, a streak of white in his hair that used to be burnished red. But his—the color returned to his face and cloak and the rest of his body.
Seeker: Whoa! You know that feeling when you walk from one room into another room, and you're like, “Was I coming in here to get a sandwich, or to just have a sandwich?” What did I miss? Something.
Riswynn: Well, the fey came after us, and now we're going after the fey.
Riswynn: You're here because we need to do something. Interplanar navigation.
Kenzo: Not to be rude to you, but how do we know that you're you, not the you that wasn't you?
DM: So how do we know? Kenzo tells us.

DM: No! You only see one aura, just Seeker's. Lady Eventide, you see, you see her curled up in a ball like she's nervous about re-entering the Feywild, or or traveling through this portal. Anyway, she's still sort of hiding there, just clustered around the streak of white hair in Seeker's—on Seeker's head.
Kenzo: Did you do that yourself, or did it just happen?

Seeker: ((Music adjustment)) She... You know, we know each other. She gave me that thread that we used. But how she ended up in the part of my hair, that's harder to explain, isn't it? Or did something happen?
DM: Color from—she took the color from your hair in exchange for the thread.
Seeker: Yes, but she didn't, at the time that occurred, possess me.
Kenzo: Well, it's good to have you back.
Kenzo: I don't know if you can give us a heads up next time, or if it's just gonna happen uncontrollably, or how does this all work?
Seeker: Well, just keep an eye out for when I wander off to get a sandwich. And maybe when I come back I'll be the lady.
Kenzo: All right. We'll establish a rigorous sandwich watch.
Seeker: I mean, fair point. I'll... I don't know. I'll try to keep an eye on it.

before: Riswynn: How responsive is Seeker right now? Oh, speaking of...
DM: Oh! Speaking of Seeker.
Kenzo: Didn't this happen last time? Didn't we, like—didn't we just, like, like, we manifested Seeker? Like, we literally said his name, and then Eric appeared.

DM: So as the Vindristjarna pulls up near the Bitterwine Oak portal: the massive oak tree, roots growing over cracked stone, growing unnaturally in the desert, seemingly unaffected by the heat; crimson pools of wine seeping from its roots into shallow basins; with pale white blossoms flowering across the tree, and brown leaves rustling in its, in its, in its branches. You see?
DM: And Faldrak calling, “Okay, we’re parked. What are you guys gonna do now?” As you're sitting on the deck talking,

lines: Delwath: Yeah, yeah, that—no, Seeker. The the fey hunters from Harrow and Wend are gonna keep coming nonstop until we do something. So it seemed like we should go do something.
Seeker: The Cloudspinner. Yes. But do what, though? Are we bringing the Cloudspinner with us to free her, or...?
Delwath: In the—what was the name of the well? The Prismwell, Prismwell, [garbled].

Delwath: But I think if we find, could find the Prismwell somewhere in the Feywild, we could maybe dip and or coat and or spin and or put Cloudspinner somehow into the Prismwell.

DM: Well, not you, probably, but the Cloudspinner, perhaps.

Riswynn: Maybe we—she could just be drawn back by her place of power.
Seeker: Well, it seems like we should go there. Yes, how is that? That's a pretty heavy giant chunk of crystal shard, isn't it, that she's entombed in?
DM: It does fit in the portable hole.

before: Seeker: What did we decide about the Crown?

Seeker: Mean, if you insist, you know, [garbled], willing to—no.

interactions.title: Ulfgar’s apocryphal realm of revelry
lines: DM: Lirien, before she died, mentioned coming via Ember—Emberwine.
Seeker: Emberwine. Wait! Do we know about that one? Oh, man.
DM: Not mentioned in it. It's not mentioned.
DM: It's not mentioned directly as a—in the fae realms, as, as something that you know, Ulfgar was confident in. But there are some stories that he dismisses as apocryphal, of...

DM: Many ancient Drankorian tales speak of a fey realm of revelry and dance. But he dismisses these as, as ancient tales, and, you know, there's no modern, no recent Chardonian confirmation of any of this.

Seeker: Well, it wouldn't be surprising that we're off the edge of our—the map produced by recent scholars. And so this journey is also a chance to add to the scholarship. Well, to learning something new! I raise a toast.

before: DM: Just, and the expanse of desert.

Seeker: Ready!
DM: And just tell—just message me the result, or if you're...

interactions.title: Tarviel notices the impossible and greets Riswynn
lines: DM: Another one reaches for Riswynn and turns when he sees Riswynn, and looks a bit surprised and says— which you actually find you do understand— “Who are you? Carries a fragment of the impossible. What are you doing here?”
Kenzo: Who's he talking to? A fragment of the impossible?
DM: “Well, then, forget the mysteries for now.”
Riswynn: I introduced myself to the one who asked me: “I’m Riswynn. Pleasure to dance in the sun with you. What’s your name?”

DM: “I am Tarviel. It is quite a joy to dance with new people. It has been so some time since such a hectic party has come through. What brings you to our land of plenty? What are you here to forget? What do you leave behind?”

Riswynn: I think I would like to forget the sorrows of Harrow and Wend.
DM: “Speak not such darkness! Here, the sun is shining, the music is playing. Why would you disturb it with tales of darkness and woe?”

before: Seeker: Hmm.
Kenzo: Okay, like, not, not, not like, you know, manipulate, like, “My, my dark plot to destroy these,” you know, type of... Yes, genuine—genuinely is having a good time.
DM: They seem to be now, at least on your surface impressions. They're having a great time.
Kenzo: You mean my deep soul sighting impression? Okay, alright, sure. Why not? I'll start dancing.
DM: “Oh, what’s stopping you? It’s been so long since we had dwarves here.”

lines: DM: One, as Seeker’s sort of creeping into the, into the corner, you know, swirling about, playing on, on her pipes, kind of moves over to you and, and starts to play sort of right in, in Seeker's face, like, pushing down on the book that you're trying to look at.

before: Wellby: Wait, I don't think we are here to forget something, right?

interactions.title: Change, a quest, and the satyrs’ farewell
lines: Delwath: We are here to bring change.
DM: She looks kind of, and stops for a moment, just ceases dancing, and everybody stops for a moment, and the music pauses.

But if we could just dance in a direction—I see that we're orbiting a single spot right now—but it can be even more fun to dance. Hey, have you ever experimented with, like, a dancing in a line? DM: Yeah, they they follow for a little bit. They seem interested. You're new and exciting. They haven't, you know... You know, they haven't—that certainly seems like they haven't seen such interesting, interesting crew in a while. So they sort of follow you dancing.
DM: You're not, like, magically compelled to dance. You could just leave.
DM: Or you can conga. You could leave.

DM: The one of the satyrs, the one who was grabbing Seeker's book and sort of chasing him around a little bit: “You wish to see the river, sample its wares. That is a joyous thing.”

Delwath: Wait, where did—where did she say?
DM: “Why do you wish to go to Everlight’s Bloom? There is nothing fun there.”

Delwath: One who perished in our world is from there, at least most recently. We wish to bring news of her passing.
Delwath: Not all things in life are fun.

DM: Kind of pouts briefly at Delwath, and sticks her tongue out. “You have lived the wrong life, then. Try a better one next time. Hmph. If you wish to bring such sad tidings, then we will dance elsewhere. Go, sour guest.”

DM: Kind of, the satyrs kind of drift off a little bit, kind of put off slightly by the news that Delwath seeks to bring, and the sound of their pipes fades slowly, leaving just the quiet buzz of the insects and the warm afternoon—late afternoon. It's really evening. It's, like, golden hour air as you begin making your way through the vineyards towards the river itself.

interactions.title: The barge master questions the party’s mission
lines: DM: And there's a—at the back, there's a, there's a man standing with, like, a big oar, who's sort of steering the barge as it slowly...

DM: And when you, when you get close enough and you sort of hail them, he calls out. He's, he's tall. He's maybe 6 feet tall. Sort of skin kind of the color of rust, sort of reddish color, but sort of almost faintly glowing. Long sort of very pale golden hair, tied back in a ponytail, wearing this like elegantly cut silver clothes, with red buttons that run up the middle of the coat.
DM: And he— he calls, calls out to you as you hail, “Travelers, what brings you to our realm?” And he begins to slow the barge slightly.

Delwath: So I'll give him a little spiel, like, apologizing for interrupting the party, and, you know, we have come here on a quest, and we are seeking his aid in getting to Everlight’s Bloom. For we have sad tidings to bring to that realm of the death of Lirien. Enter Golden Stag, or something like that. I’ll give her some of her titles, right? Recite some of Lirien’s titles. Can you direct us, or help us, or assist us in any way? We would greatly appreciate the— anything you could do to speed us on our journey.
DM: He looks kind of—his, his face falls a little bit. He looks... He looks slightly disappointed.

DM: “And here I thought you had come to join us on the Last Draught for our voyage to the Sunwine Halls. And yet you say you will leave this land for the bright stasis of Everlight’s Bloom. Such a tragedy. Are you sure you would not hear our tale?”
Delwath: Our duty calls, unfortunately. Cannot be shaken from our quest.
DM: “The Golden Prince cares not for those who leave. What makes you believe he will wish tidings of this Lirien? You said her name was.”

DM: He looks kind of, you know, askance at you.

DM: But sort of shrugs his shoulders. “Huh! Will not press into the business of strange travelers. But, hmm, I guess if you seek Everlight’s Bloom, just follow the river. If your mission is true, your steps will be quick. You must have been to Everlight’s Bloom before, yes?”
DM: He looks kind of surprised to hear that.
DM: He looks. He gives you—as this, the— the barge master gives you this sort of strange look, like something's clearly not adding up with your story.
DM: “The—do you have to... Prince’s desires are his own, and should he wish a stranger to bring him tidings of one who left his land? If you truly are on a...”
DM: Kind of shakes his head.
DM: “I will not stop the will of the lords. Let your feet carry you where they may.”
DM: Kind of mutters to himself, “Foolish mortals!”
DM: “I bid you a fond afternoon and pleasant journeys.”
DM: Kind of shakes his head a little bit, pushes off.

DM: The pot—the apron is gone. She's clearly washed her hands, paws. She's sort of, like, combed her hair a little bit.
DM: “Travelers! Yes, thanks. So feel free to set it down.” And she just kind of reaches behind her and drags a table out from somewhere.
DM: “Come, come, sit, relax, tell me, why are you here?”
Wellby: This is inside the house or in front of the house?
DM: In front of the house.
DM: She's, like, pulling chairs out. She, like—it's like clowns coming out of the car.

Wellby: You know we've gotten a little bit turned around here. Oh, where— Where are we right now?

DM: “Where are you? Well, of course, that is the question, isn’t it? Well, you're in late afternoon, as you can see. Another way you might put it is Emberwine. You know that place? Yes, you’ve— you’ve been here before? No, you look a bit stunned by the Feywild, I might say. Have some pie.” She starts cutting it up.
DM: “You’re at Auntie Mulberry’s house. Of course, you must have known that, appearing here out of nowhere like that, with a boom and a thud and a crash of breaking glass. What was that all about?”
Wellby: But Wellby telepathically says to Kenzo, “Soul Sight.”

DM: No, no, it—I... So you're only aware of its basic emotional state. It doesn't, like, give you, you know, deep secrets or anything like that, just to be clear. She's super curious about visitors, pretty cheerful and happy.
DM: “Pie, come, come. Don’t be ungracious guests. I baked it for you.”
Wellby: It is so thoughtful of you. I am absolutely stuffed right now. I wish I could, and I... I just can't.
DM: “So why have you come, then, and disturbed my peaceful rest, if not to have a cheerful meal and tell us some tales?”
Wellby: Wellby looks over at Delwath at this point.
Delwath: Well, well, we’re always happy to share some tales. Okay, he starts absent-mindedly eating a slice of pie. Go on. What sort of tale would you like to hear, a happy tale or a sad tale?
DM: “Oh, a happy tale! Nobody tells sad tales in Emberwine.”
Delwath: Well Delwath pauses for a minute. Even the happy tales are full of sadness.
DM: “You must not be a good storyteller, then.”
Delwath: Well, the stories from our lives are forced, the— come out a certain way, given how our lives have gone! Would you like a made up story?
DM: “Speak, speak! I’m waiting. Pie’s getting cold.” She’s eating.
Delwath: Delwath, Delwath will tell the tale of the killing of the warlord, killing Grash,
Delwath: And the orcs, the free orcs, and their, their freedom from Thark at the hands of the Cloudspinner’s cloak.
DM: As she’s listening, she sort of turns over, and she nudges Wellby. “Be a dear, Wellby, go get the tea, please. I can hear the kettle whistling.”
Wellby: Yeah. Yeah. Yep, yep. You know, being as small as I am, I may need a second set of hands. Kenzo? Yeah, okay, we'll go. Yeah, yeah.
Kenzo: Sounds good, did the thing.
Wellby: The door—I definitely give you a glance, like, “We’re gonna die. We’re gonna die, right?”
DM: “Get the tray of cookies from the oven, too, please.”
Kenzo: Seems, Tim—she seems harmless, right? Like, that she's very sincere, right, like...
Wellby: Introduce ourselves? Or did she just know our names without having introduced ourselves?
Kenzo: Like reading our minds and stuff.
Wellby: Yep, that's reading our minds.
DM: I mean, obviously a little obviously suspicious. Doesn't take a mind reader.
DM: “Yes, go on. The elf is a good storyteller. Come, bring my tea before his tale is done.”
Kenzo: Kenzo asks telepathically just things like, “What’s your favorite number?”
Wellby: You go in—you go into the house?
Kenzo: Go into the house. But I—but I’m thinking, “What’s your favorite—what’s your favorite cookie?”
Wellby: Me, too. I’ll say to Delwath, you know, “If we’re not back in 2 min, assume something’s gone catastrophically wrong.”

DM: So Wellby would notice, like, the house looks subtly different. Like, it's smaller, it's more cramped when you're looking—when she was standing in the doorway, and you're looking through the house, through the door of the house, like, you couldn't...

DM: You couldn't, like—it didn't—the spatial arrangement didn't really make sense. Like, you couldn't see the back. You couldn't. But now it just looks like a 1—like a 2 room cottage, right? You're in the kitchen of a small little cottage.

DM: There's a curtain behind a door that clearly leads to, like, a bedroom or something. There's a, like, a big iron stove with a fire going in it, and there's a kettle on it. There's like a, like a, you know, bread baking, or sweets baking, sweet buns baking inside the oven that you pull out. You... Kettle's hot. You pour some tea. Seems very normal.
Wellby: Alright! We'll take it back out again.

Kenzo: Unfortunately, a lot of our tales feature a lot of death.

Kenzo: We're the sky crawlers of Vindristjarna.
Kenzo: Yeah, sorry. I was—not that good?
DM: “You have potential for some things. So, a nice story, lovely to hear. Now, what?”

interactions.title: Invitations, allies, and a guide
lines: Riswynn: What's our potential for reaching another way to Everlight’s Bloom from here?
DM: “Why would you want to do that?”
Riswynn: We heard it's ever light.
DM: “Yeah, same way a glass lamp shining on a bug trapped in glass is ever light. I mean, if you wish to go, do you—you have an invitation from the Prince, I assume?”

DM: “Golden Prince, the Hearthkeeper, Lord of Everlight’s Bloom, T.”
DM: “I am not so joyless as to be friends with one such as him. What do you take me for?”
Wellby: What's a good way to get an introduction?
DM: She sort of stops talking for a minute, like chewing her pie slowly.
DM: Like, her voice turns a little bit more serious and sort of less jokey and cheerful.
Riswynn: We're traveling a voyage in reverse from a fae that we met in our realm. She came through here from Everlight’s Bloom, so we wanted to go from here to Everlight’s Bloom.
Riswynn: Wanted to know more about her and the people who knew her there. Seems like it would be a good story.
Seeker: Seeker picks up a fork and starts to grab a morsel of the pie and looks at it, kind of shakes his head.
Seeker: Looks a little bit, a little bit glassy eyed, puts it back down.
Seeker: Bye, I, I gotta go.
Kenzo: Color begins to fade from Seeker's head.

DM: As the color begins to fade slowly from Seeker, initially seemingly not something that Auntie Mulberry notices, she turns and looks at Riswynn, and, like, does a bit of a double take, looking at Riswynn again.

DM: “Golden Prince does not favor those who leave his realm. Everlight’s Bloom is ever light. Yes, light’s warm, golden, eternal, but after a time, even the gold can feel like a cage. I do not know that he would wish to speak with you. If you are simply bringing news of one who fled, what care is it to him?”
Delwath: We are seeking allies. They seem in short supply here in Emberwine.

DM: “Maybe you are just not trusting enough, my friend elf. I see none of you have bothered to consume my pie except for your friend dwarf over here. How do you expect anybody to trust you if you will not trust anybody to begin with? Come, you have rejected my hospitality. Why would you expect me to be your ally?”
DM: “Well, if you don’t look for allies, of course you’ll never find them.”
DM: She starts laughing, takes a sip of her tea. [garbled]
DM: “This’ll make a good story for the tales of the Feywild, I can tell. Tromps around complaining there are no allies, and insists on never looking for them. A lovely tale.”
DM: “No, sorry, seriously, not to make fun. Allies are everywhere. You just gotta try. You wish to make the ally of your—an ally of the Prince.”
DM: “Your tale was nice. It is worth some help. I will overlook your rudeness, I guess.”
Riswynn: Has anything happened to Seeker other than his usual colorless fading?
Delwath: Those we have met in Emberwine seem inward and withdrawn in the pursuit of their own pleasures. Not occur to us that there would be someone willing to look beyond that here.
DM: Is it, like, you know...
DM: “Well, nobody is going to go on your full quest with you, my friend, but neither will the Golden Prince. What do you wish an ally for?”
DM: “You appeared out of nowhere. You don’t seem to need help in magic.”
Delwath: No, we are quite skilled.
DM: “Why are you seeking an ally?”

Riswynn: Well, despite unfortunately appearing rude to you due to not being hungry for pie at the moment, we honestly don't want to disturb any customs or tread where we're not invited. And so we need allies if we're to travel, to be permitted to... Mean...
Wellby: And we need a guide. We don't...
Wellby: Exactly know how to get to the places where we're going.
DM: “A guide! Well, now, that is a very different thing than an ally, is it not? You wish to find something.”
Wellby: One hopes the guide is not an enemy.
DM: “Such a mortal perspective on things. I am neither your enemy nor your ally. I am Auntie Mulberry. So what do you want?”

DM: “I will do what I can in exchange for the elf’s tale, despite the death. It was a good one. You told it well, your voice is sweet, my friend. It would be sweeter with some pie, but it is sweet. But you seem to know not what you wish to ask.”

Riswynn: I appreciate that, what you have told us about the Lord of Everlight’s Bloom. We did not, for example, know that we needed an invitation to be in his land, and that is the sort of thing that we want a guide to help us to be respectful of the ways of each place. But we want to travel freely in the Feywild, and...
Riswynn: We want a guide who knows the limitations we might face.
Delwath: More than that, we came here to bring change like there hasn't been in hundreds of years.
DM: “Oh, now, that is an arrogant thing to say, my friend. Doubt you can change Emberwine.”
Delwath: We are looking for those who would benefit from these changes.
DM: “Oh, very mysterious! He’s a secretive elf. How would you find some who would benefit without saying what change you would bring?”
Delwath: Wow! If you were clever enough, you might be able to have guessed what I was hinting at.
DM: “I have never been clever in my whole life. I bake well, which you would know if you would eat my pie. Come, why so antagonistic?”
Kenzo: Kenzo eats some of the pie.
DM: How is it? It's really good.
Delwath: How is the pie, Kenzo?
DM: Mulberry pie, with, like, just the right amount of sugar balanced with tartness. Still warm, somehow.
Kenzo: “Pretty fucking good.” Kenzo, like, starts really digging in.
DM: She sort of leans over, rabbit ears are sort of twitching a little bit, like big smile beaming on her face.
Kenzo: Tim, I'm not, like, getting cursed or charmed, or anything weird that’s happening?
DM: Not, not that you're aware of.
Kenzo: Man, I'm pretty aware. It's 1 of my things. Yeah, I just keep eating. I'm really enjoying myself.
Riswynn: 1st people we spoke of in Everlight's Bloom, of the problems we perceive, did not want to talk about dark things, so we became shy of speaking of the change we want to bring.
DM: “No one likes dark tales. I do not want to hear of dark things either. Even your happy tales are a bit dark.”
Riswynn: What if the change you want to bring is to make there be fewer dark tales, or turn a dark tale into a happy one?

interactions.title: A refugee, the Cloudspinner’s return, and a guiding melody
lines: Riswynn: ((Player suggestion)) Riswynn says, “If, yeah, Emberwine is far from dark things that trouble you, and Everlight’s Bloom likewise keeps the dark away, what is the geography of the places in the fae where darkness is happening, and the residents would like to change that? Can you tell us where are the lands with dark problems? You don’t have to talk about what they are. You don’t have to go there, but can you share the geography of...”
DM: And, and pats, like, Riswynn on that.
DM: “Dear, dear! I’m sorry now, I seem to have scared you. You don’t have to be quite so nervous. I don’t bite.”
DM: “Well, Amberglow’s to the north, way to the north. Bit hard to cross these days. Not sure anybody really properly lives there anymore.”
DM: Just sort of shakes her shoulders a little bit.

DM: “Everlight’s Bloom is, like, westish, sun sunward of here. It’s all bright and cheery and bright and bright, and nothing ever changes there. You know, if a flower always blooms in Everbloom, you never get fruit. Thought about that? In this case.”
Riswynn: Anticipation of the bud, myself. Such a hopeful thing, a bud.

DM: “Sorry, thinking about something else. What? What did you ask? What’s around here? I mean, that’s about all it is. I mean, across the Sunset Gate, that’s Hollowdark, and all those sorts of nasty things we don’t talk about in polite society.”
DM: “Towards sunset, yeah, just don’t cross the gate.”
Delwath: If we were looking for somebody who knew Amberglow and cared about Amberglow, where would we find such a person?
DM: Kind of shakes her head.
DM: “Sad tales again, my dear elf. Sad tales, right at my table, and you don’t eat my pie.”
DM: Kind of shakes her head.
DM: “So you wish to find one to replace the one who died?”
Delwath: Who said anybody about dying—said anything about dying?
DM: “You just did. You said she died.”
Delwath: We knew somebody. I guess maybe.
Riswynn: Yes, she could have been our guide.
Riswynn: We thought of her as more than that. But yes, she could have been our guide.
DM: “That is not easy, my friend. Not easy.”
DM: “Most of those who still survive... I guess I don’t know.”

DM: She then kind of smiles, and, and: “Well, no, I did hear that there is a refugee from Cloudspinner’s Court at Sunwine Hall, court of the Master of the Revels. Lord Soven, you must know him. You’re in his land. I don’t know if he would help you, as people come to— people come here to forget, you know.”
Delwath: Yes, as I said, we've struggled to get people who would be interested in helping here. Hence our uncertainty about asking you.
Wellby: How would we find our way to that hall?
DM: “Oh, just...” She looks to the south.

DM: “If you wish— come to the master, the party of the Master of the Revels, your feet will take you there quite quickly. I am told it requires a little bit of a dance, hop, and a skip. Dance your way to the music.”
Wellby: Alright, we can do that.

DM: “Oh, yes, they’re always dancing, dancing, and singing. They eat my pie. They come by quite frequently, actually. Sometimes I think it’s all they eat. If that is where you wish to go, then yes, that is an easy place to get to. If you would prefer to find your way to Everlight’s Bloom, I’m not saying I cannot help. But don’t expect Prince Aurelian to eagerly await the news of this person you spoke of. Did you tell her her name?”
Delwath: Yeah. But would Prince Aurelian care about change on his borders? Wait, does he border... She said... He doesn't even border Amberglow, right? Necessarily.
DM: “He does. He borders both Emberwine and Amberglow.”
DM: She kind of shakes her head.

DM: “Not sure you quite understand. Nothing that happens in Amberglow will change Everlight’s Bloom. I mean, maybe if the Cloudspinner were alive, I guess, but not because that would change anything. Only because, well, she was always— people say. Anyway, it was before my time. She kind of, she's stronger than anybody else around: Lord Egan, Lord Soven, Prince Aurelian. None of them are a queen.”
Delwath: Said we were coming to bring change unlike any anybody has seen in hundreds of years.

DM: “You realize if what you’re hinting at is true, nobody would prefer the rivers of darkness from Darkfall and Hollowdark to the Cloudspinner’s return, you fool! You really think everybody would like to see the Sunset Gate crack and Harrow and Wend march across our lands? Have you been keeping secret some mystery to how to restore the Cloudspinner?”
Wellby: You don't think the Lords would prefer to go on being lords without a queen over them, or nearby, anyway?
DM: She kind of mutters: “It is not for me to say what archfey would do, but the Queen of Sunsets is better than Harrow and Wend. Nobody can deny that. What do you think we’re trying to forget here?”
Delwath: And Harrow and Wend and others have their agents. Why do you think we're being cautious?
DM: “Just eat the pie.” Kind of shakes her head, looks up at the sky.
Riswynn: Who's eaten pie so far? Just Seeker and Kenzo?
DM: “I will do you a favor, as I promised, for your story was true, but I grow weary.”
Wellby: Which direction are we headed?
Delwath: I think we should go to the Sunwine Hall.
Wellby: I agree, get info from the refugee person.

DM: She kind of stands up and, and pushes her chair back, reaches into her pocket, and, like, brings out, like, a small, like a pocket... She's got—she's wearing, like, a skirt that's got pockets in it, and reaches in. She brings out a small, what looks like a little, like, flute, like pan, like little bird whistle type thing.
DM: She blows into it and sort of spins it around.
DM: “Melody will lead you there. Just dance.”
Riswynn: Thank you for all you've taught us, and for the tune.
